rationale: The retained execution of the fixed probe confirms the event-backpressure defect, so the question moves to an asserted defect claim; in parallel it registers the next independent sourced lead on the core's accept-phase progress (no resend of Accepted/AcceptDecide).

investigations.question: In the core Sequence Paxos, if a follower's Accepted reply (or the leader's AcceptDecide) is lost, does any timer-driven or self-initiated mechanism restore the leader's knowledge of that acceptance, or does a quorum-accepted entry stay undecided until an unrelated new proposal arrives?
investigations.hypothesis: There is no repair for this direction: resend_messages_leader in Phase::Accept only resends a pending StopSign/its decide and re-Prepares peers that are not promised, and resend_messages_follower in Phase::Accept is an empty arm, so a lost Accepted is never retried by either side; the leader's decision only re-evaluates on a later handle_accepted, i.e. only when some follower accepts something new, which requires an unrelated proposal.
investigations.discriminator: A deterministic in-process simulation (real OmniPaxos instances with a memory storage, manual message delivery and logical ticks): elect a leader, propose one entry, let the follower accept it, drop only that follower's Accepted, then keep ticking and delivering for a fair window with no new proposals, and compare the leader's decided_idx against a control run in which the same message is delivered. If the entry stays undecided in the drop case while both the leader's own acceptance and the follower's accepted_idx show a quorum, the loss is repaired by nothing in that interval; if the entry becomes decided without the message or without a new proposal, the hypothesis is refuted.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled mechanism: the actor publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor builds as `async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity)` (handle.rs:295-323; knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that never consumes the event stream still leaves it unread, and `subscribe_events` only hands out clones of that same channel (handle.rs:254-259). A `send` that cannot fit parks the actor task, which then cannot run `op.tick()` (election heartbeats, resends, batch flushes), cannot handle incoming messages, and cannot answer any Command - including the `append_notify` Timeout that `drain_notifiers` would have produced on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222; endpoint documented at handle.rs:114-137). The crate's sibling egress paths avoid exactly this with `try_send` (drain_outgoing_buf; push_to_sub/push_to_all_subs) and its own regression test states the invariant for the outgoing channel. Recorded execution 011decb17a314e839b860436ad3dc164 (experiment 9a11299aa4344bb5b84565cbe33701ad-experiment, exit 0) ran the two-case harness against the clean copy and its test_selection reports both cases passed: `unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop` and `drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running` (nothing filtered out). Case 1 (event_capacity 64, paced 4ms proposals, no consumer) required and observed: all three event channels full (`len == capacity`, receiver not closed), at least one node whose actor never answered a `decided_idx` command across ten 200ms samples and still answered nothing 500ms later, and that node's `append_notify_with_timeout(.., 300ms)` unresolved after 4s although its `append_notify_timeout` is 1500ms. Case 2 (identical cluster, capacity and activity, with a task draining each event stream) required and observed the opposite: every node kept answering commands and a follower `append_notify` resolved `Ok(idx >= 1)`. Because the only difference between the cases is whether the event stream is consumed, the parking and the withheld endpoints are attributed to the unconsumed bounded event channel, not to the transport, the configuration or the harness. Scope of the defect asserted: a node whose client does not consume its event stream permanently stops participating (no ticks, no message handling, no command replies) once it has observed `event_capacity` transitions, for any finite capacity - the probe reaches that bound at 64 to stay inside a bounded window, and the source-settled mechanism is capacity-independent. Counter-limitations, kept in force: (a) the trigger is client-side usage and no snapshot source states a drain obligation, so the defect rests on the handle-method contract (every Command reply, and the documented Timeout) plus the deliberate non-blocking design of the sibling egress paths; (b) a receiver that is dropped unblocks the actor (the send error is ignored), so the stall lasts exactly as long as a live receiver exists; (c) the receipt witnesses the bound at 64 with node-local endpoints only - no observation at the 1024 default and no quorum-level measurement of the other nodes losing this participant; (d) the receipt has no parsed events (the harness asserts rather than emitting event lines), so its decisive content is the two recorded test outcomes, not parsed indices. That receipt recorded no parsed observations (event_count 0), so it cannot be cited as completed support and this account stays conditional: the defect is asserted on the source plus that recorded run, and a revised harness emitting CA_EVENT operands was submitted for a fresh execution so a later account can cite parsed indices.
limitations: Capacity-independence and practical reachability at the default 1024 are argued from source, not observed: the execution reached the bound at event_capacity=64.

Only node-local endpoints are witnessed (command round-trips and the append_notify endpoint); the consequence for the rest of the cluster (lost quorum participant, leadership churn caused by the silent node) is not measured.
The receipt carries no parsed events (event_count 0), so no zero-based indices are available for it; the decisive record is the receipt's test outcomes.

The stalled-consumer variant from earlier construction is superseded as evidence: its non-freeze was traced to proposals being decided inside a single tick gap, which coalesced transitions; the retained probe paces proposals instead.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only current account of the new question, no execution yet. A follower replies to each AcceptDecide/AcceptStopSign with an Accepted that carries only the receipt's ballot and the follower's accepted_idx (follower.rs:160-175), and the leader turns those receipts into a decision when `is_chosen` sees a quorum of advertised accepted indexes (leader.rs:316-345). Both roles have a periodic callback - SequencePaxos::resend_message_timeout dispatches to resend_messages_leader/resend_messages_follower every resend_message_tick_timeout logical ticks (mod.rs:229-246) - but in the accept phase the leader's version only resends a pending StopSign (or its decide) and re-Prepares peers that are not promised (leader.rs:371-403), and the follower's version is the empty `Phase::Accept => ()` arm (follower.rs:240-269); the follower's other periodic path, flush_batch_follower, replies only when the batch flush itself advanced the accepted index (follower.rs:284-290). So the direction follower->leader has no timer-driven retry, and the leader has no way to ask a follower for its accepted index; the only later trigger is a new AcceptDecide arriving for new entries, which makes the follower advertise a (possibly larger) accepted_idx. Whether that leaves a genuinely quorum-accepted entry undecided for an unbounded interval with no enabled repair under normal (no further proposal) conditions is exactly what the registered discriminator is to decide; no defect is claimed before it runs.
limitations: The claim depends on the environment being permitted to lose a single message while the transport keeps the rest in order; the probe must drop only the Accepted reply and keep delivering everything else.

A retry of the client's own proposal (in the runtime layer) can repair the earlier entry as a side effect, so any later assertion must be scoped to 'no further proposal is made', which the core API does not itself require of a caller.

experiment.revision_reason: Same probe, cluster/configuration and the same two cases, but the harness now prints CA_EVENT JSON lines with the observed operands (bound reached, parked node, withheld endpoint, control responsiveness, control append_notify) so the receipt carries parsed observations a conclusion can cite; the previous receipt ran both cases green but recorded no parsed events.
experiment.prefix: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) built with OmniPaxosConfig::build over omnipaxos_storage::memory_storage::MemoryStorage, each driven by a real omnipaxos_runtime actor from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one in-process transport task per node forwards each message from that node's outgoing_messages() to msg.get_receiver()'s handle_incoming. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, event_capacity 64, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, flush_batch_tick_timeout 100. Ordinary appends are paced at 4ms so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks; a burst would decide many entries inside one tick gap and emit a single amalgamated event. Case unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop leaves each node's event receiver unread (the handle owns one from spawn_actor even if the application never calls subscribe_events) and emits CA_EVENT unconsumed_event_bound_reached {nodes_full,nodes,event_capacity}, CA_EVENT actor_parked {node,samples_without_reply,reply_budget_ms,permanently_parked} and CA_EVENT append_notify_endpoint_withheld {node,per_call_deadline_ms,actor_timeout_ms,outer_wait_ms,resolved}. Case drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running is the control with one difference, a task per node draining the same stream, and emits CA_EVENT control_actors_responsive {nodes_answering,nodes,event_capacity} and CA_EVENT control_append_notify {origin,succeeded,idx}.

scope.description: Bounded probe of whether an event stream the application does not consume (bounded by RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) parks the single actor loop and withholds its command/append_notify endpoints, with a drained-stream control in the same execution.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum, no message loss or reordering beyond the in-process transport, one tokio runtime in one process
event_capacity 64 so the bound is reached inside a bounded window; the source-settled mechanism (send awaits when the channel holds event_capacity events) is capacity-independent
the handle's event receiver exists from construction, so an application that never subscribes still leaves it unread
excluded: schedule independence or any rate bound
